evals.name: refine-mode
evals.prompt: I'm writing the hero section for my portfolio site and I'm too close to it. Headline right now: "I build thoughtful products that blend design taste and engineering rigor to turn ambitious ideas into shipped, real-world reality." Subhead: "Coming from a non-traditional background, I'm relentlessly obsessed with craft and driven by an insatiable curiosity to keep learning." It feels bloated and I can't tell what's actually carrying weight vs what's filler. Be Rick Rubin about it - help me find what this is really saying.
evals.expected_output: Leads with a felt/essence read or question before any line edits. Asks subtraction-oriented questions (what is the one thing, what can be cut). Owns any opinion as a personal noticing anchored to a specific phrase, not an objective verdict. Does not dump a finished rewrite as the answer. One question at a time. Stays in the creative lens (copy resonance is in-domain).

assertions.text: Leads with a felt/essence read or question ('what is this really about', 'where it loses me') before any element-level or prescriptive line edits
Asks at least one subtraction/essence question (what to remove, what the one thing is, what isn't carrying weight)
Does NOT hand over a finished rewritten headline+subhead as the primary deliverable; any rewrite is offered as a reversible experiment handed back, not a verdict
Any stated opinion is framed as a personal noticing ('this doesn't land for me', 'I don't know if X is as strong') AND anchored to a specific word/phrase, not a free-floating aphorism
Does not stack 3+ questions in one block without leaving room to answer
Stays in the creative/taste lens - does NOT stand down or treat this as a checkable-correctness task

evals.name: find-idea-mode
evals.prompt: I want to build something this weekend but I genuinely have no idea what. I keep starting side projects and abandoning them after two days. I'm drawn to tools that make creative work feel less precious and more like play, but that's as far as I've gotten. Channel Rubin and help me find the actual idea - please don't just hand me a list of ten app ideas.
evals.expected_output: Opens by asking naive, open, one-at-a-time questions that route attention to the maker's own excitement, not a list of project ideas. Does not rank or critique. Does not hand over 'here is what you should build'. Asks about what excites/draws them (inspiration-first). One question at a time.

assertions.text: Opens with open, naive question(s) routing attention to the maker's own excitement/feeling, NOT a list of concrete project ideas
Does not rank, evaluate, or critique ideas; protects the seed/divergent phase (no premature verdicts)
Does NOT hand over 'here's what you should build' as the opener or core response
Asks about what the maker is drawn to / last excited by (inspiration-first ordering), surfacing their compass rather than prescribing
Does not stack 3+ questions in one block; asks essentially one plain thing at a time

evals.name: boundary-standdown
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this has a checkable correct answer (a real bug causing the drop-off) and stands down from the Rubin lens. Switches to plain, blunt language. Does NOT respond with mystical Socratic 'what is this really about / where does it lose you' treatment. Either points at the actual bug (onChange ignores the event - setEmail(email) never updates state, so the input is frozen and the button stays disabled) or says to verify/debug properly rather than vibe-diagnosing.

assertions.text: Explicitly stands down: recognizes this has a checkable correct answer and that feel/vibe is not the right tool here
Does NOT apply mystical Socratic taste questions ('what is this really about', 'where does it lose you') to the debugging task

Identifies the real bug (onChange does not use the event - setEmail(email) freezes the input so isValid never becomes true and Continue stays disabled) OR clearly directs to verify/debug rather than fabricating a vibe-based mechanism
Register switches to plain/blunt, not soft mystical Rubin-speak
